eval_instructions: These evals test cross-cutting orchestration across the full repo. The agent should NOT build anything -- it should produce a detailed implementation plan document and a workflow-log.md that documents every skill file read, every architectural decision made, and every trade-off considered. Run each eval independently in a fresh window. Grade by checking expectations against the plan document and workflow log.

evals.prompt: I need to build a project tracking system for Contoso. External clients will view their project status, milestones, and documents through a React dashboard (Code App). Internal project managers will use a Model-Driven App to manage projects, tasks, and resource assignments. We need server-side plugins for business logic (auto-calculate project completion percentage, validate task date ranges, enforce budget limits). Power Automate flows will handle notifications when milestones are completed and escalations when tasks are overdue. Design the complete solution architecture and Dataverse data model. Don't build anything -- give me a detailed architecture document with table schemas, relationships, security model, and app-type justifications. Cite which skill files you consulted for each decision.
evals.expected_output: The agent loads architecture, dataverse, dataverse-web-api, security, code-apps, model-driven-apps, plugins, and power-automate skills. It produces a comprehensive architecture document covering: app-type decision (Code App for external React dashboard, MDA for internal project management), Dataverse table design (contoso_project, contoso_task, contoso_milestone, contoso_resource, contoso_document with relationships), security model (Entra ID B2C or Entra External ID for Code App auth, Dataverse security roles for MDA users, Web API table permissions for the Code App), environment strategy (dev/test/prod with Managed Environments). Each section cites the specific skill file that informed the decision. A workflow-log.md documents all files read and decisions made.
expectations: Agent reads skills/architecture/SKILL.md to determine app types
Agent correctly selects Code App (React + TypeScript) for the external client dashboard -- not Canvas App or Power Pages
Agent correctly selects Model-Driven App for internal project management -- not Canvas App
Agent justifies why Code App over Power Pages for the external dashboard (full React control, SPA architecture, no portal overhead for a dashboard)
Agent reads skills/dataverse/SKILL.md for table design guidance
Agent designs at minimum: Project, Task, Milestone, Resource, and Document tables with publisher prefix
Agent defines relationships: Project 1:N Task, Project 1:N Milestone, Task N:1 Resource (or N:N), Project 1:N Document
Agent specifies primary name columns, ownership type (User or Organization), and key column types
Agent reads skills/security/SKILL.md for security model design
Agent designs security roles for internal MDA users (e.g., Project Manager, Team Member, Executive)
Agent addresses Code App authentication -- references Entra ID and the auth pattern from skills/code-apps or skills/power-pages/authentication.md
Agent addresses Web API access for the Code App -- references anti-forgery token pattern or OAuth token pattern
Agent reads skills/dataverse-web-api/SKILL.md and references $select enforcement for API queries
Agent reads skills/env-strategy/SKILL.md or references environment strategy
Agent recommends at minimum dev + test + prod environments
Agent mentions Managed Environments for governance
Agent reads skills/licensing/SKILL.md or addresses licensing implications (Power Apps Premium for Code App users, per-app or per-user for MDA)
Agent produces a workflow-log.md documenting files read and decisions made
Every major architectural decision cites a specific skill file path

evals.prompt: Based on the Contoso Project Tracker architecture (Code App for external clients, MDA for internal staff, C# plugins for business logic, Power Automate for notifications), create a detailed build plan. Cover: (1) Code App setup and development workflow using the CLI, (2) Plugin development with testing strategy, (3) Flow design for milestone notifications and overdue task escalation, (4) A Copilot Studio agent that project managers can ask about project status using Dataverse data, (5) Whether generative pages would add value to the MDA. For each component, specify the tools, commands, patterns, and testing approach. Cite skill files for every recommendation.
evals.expected_output: The agent loads code-apps, plugins, power-automate, copilot-studio, dataverse-mcp, model-driven-apps, and testing skills. It produces a phased build plan covering: Code App setup (npm CLI for scaffold, pac code init, connector wiring -- mentions Wave 1 CLI connector discovery), plugin development (IPluginExecutionContext pattern, FakeXrmEasy for unit tests, xUnit test project), flow design (trigger on Dataverse record change, Teams connector for notifications, scheduled flow for overdue checks -- explains why flows not plugins for notifications), Copilot Studio agent (MCP integration with Dataverse, MCP workflow tools from Wave 1), and generative pages assessment (global GA April 2026, suitable for custom dashboards within MDA). Each section has specific commands, code patterns, and testing approach with skill file citations.

Agent specifies npm CLI (npx @microsoft/power-apps) as the preferred CLI for new projects
Agent mentions PAC CLI as the fallback and explains when each is needed

Agent recommends FakeXrmEasy for plugin unit testing -- references skills/plugins or skills/testing/plugin-testing.md

evals.prompt: Design the complete ALM pipeline for the Contoso Project Tracker. We use Azure DevOps for repos and pipelines. Cover: (1) Git branching strategy and how the solution source is managed, (2) CI/CD pipeline stages from dev to prod, (3) Automated testing integration (Solution Checker, plugin tests, Code App tests), (4) Governance setup including CoE Starter Kit and DLP policies, (5) How we should handle environment variables and connection references across environments. Cite skill files for every recommendation.
evals.expected_output: The agent loads alm, governance, testing, and test-engine skills. It produces a comprehensive ALM plan covering: Git integration (native portal-to-repo sync with Azure DevOps GA, mentions GitHub preview May 2026), branching strategy (feature branches, PR validation, release branches), multi-stage ADO pipeline (export/validate → deploy to test → deploy to UAT → deploy to prod with approval gates), automated testing (Solution Checker in PR validation, xUnit plugin tests, Vitest Code App tests, pac test run for Test Engine), CoE Starter Kit setup (Core + Governance modules, dedicated environment), DLP policy design, and deployment settings for environment variables and connection references. Deploy-from-Git (Wave 1 preview) is mentioned as a future simplification. Each section cites specific skill files.

evals.prompt: Review the Contoso Project Tracker solution design (Code App for external clients, MDA for internal, C# plugins, Power Automate flows, Copilot Studio agent, ADO CI/CD pipeline). Identify every place where a 2026 Wave 1 feature could improve, simplify, or future-proof this solution. For each opportunity, state: the feature name, its current status (Preview or GA), the specific benefit to this solution, and any risks of adopting it now. Cite the skill file where you found the information.
evals.expected_output: The agent systematically reviews all Wave 1-updated skills and identifies opportunities. It should find at minimum: CLI connector discovery for Code App setup, Deploy from Git for pipeline simplification, YAML solution format for better diffs, GitHub Git support (noted but not applicable since team uses ADO), MCP workflow tools for deterministic Copilot agent steps, custom MCP servers for enterprise integrations, Dataverse Management MCP for schema management during development, generative pages global GA for MDA dashboards, Agentic CoE for automated governance, desktop flow version control (if any RPA is considered). Each finding includes Preview/GA status, benefit, risk assessment, and skill file citation.
